### 💡 Codex Review Here are some automated review suggestions for this pull request. **Reviewed commit:** `8702c822da`
ℹ️ About Codex in GitHub
[Your team has set up Codex to review pull requests in this repo](http://chatgpt.com/codex/settings/general). Reviews are triggered when you - Open a pull request for review - Mark a draft as ready - Comment "@codex review". If Codex has suggestions, it will comment; otherwise it will react with 👍. Codex can also answer questions or update the PR. Try commenting "@codex address that feedback".

**Actionable comments posted: 3**
🧹 Nitpick comments (2)
scripts/generate_test_audio.ts (1)
`33-33`: **Unhandled promise rejection on top-level call.** The `.catch(console.error)` logs the error but the process will exit with code 0 even on failure. Consider propagating the error to the exit code.
Proposed fix ```diff -generateTestAudio().catch(console.error); +generateTestAudio().catch(err => { + console.error(err); + process.exit(1); +}); ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. In `@scripts/generate_test_audio.ts` at line 33, Top-level call to generateTestAudio() uses .catch(console.error) which logs errors but leaves process exit code as 0; change the invocation to propagate failures by handling the error and exiting with non-zero code — e.g. replace generateTestAudio().catch(console.error) with an explicit handler that logs the error (console.error or processLogger) and calls process.exit(1), or invoke generateTestAudio inside an async IIFE and catch errors to call process.exit(1); reference the generateTestAudio invocation to locate the change. ```
scripts/e2e.ts (1)
`68-73`: **Fixed timeout for hydration is fragile.** Using `waitForTimeout(2000)` for hydration is a time-based assumption that may be too short on slow CI runners or unnecessarily slow on fast machines. Consider waiting for a specific element or network idle state.
Proposed fix ```diff await page.goto(appUrl); - // Wait for hydration - await page.waitForTimeout(2000); + await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle'); ```
🤖 Prompt for AI Agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. In `@scripts/e2e.ts` around lines 68 - 73, Replace the fragile time-based hydration wait (page.waitForTimeout) with a deterministic wait: after page.goto(appUrl) use a specific readiness signal such as await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle') or await page.waitForSelector('') so tests only proceed once the app has actually hydrated; update the code around page.goto and page.waitForTimeout to call page.waitForLoadState or waitForSelector with a meaningful selector (e.g., the app root or a known hydrated element). ```
🤖 Prompt for all review comments with AI agents ``` Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed. Inline comments: In `@scripts/e2e.ts`: - Around line 138-142: The catch block in the top-level run (where errors are logged via console.error('Test failed:', err)) doesn't set a non-zero exit code, so failures still return success; modify the catch/finally flow in the e2e runner to ensure the process exits with a failure status (e.g., call process.exit(1) or rethrow the error after ensuring browser.close() in finally) when an exception is caught, referencing the existing catch(err) handler and the finally block that awaits browser.close() so the browser is closed before exiting. - Around line 6-10: The runTests function must validate required prerequisites: ensure process.env.DEEPGRAM_API_KEY is present and that the audioFile path (const audioFile) points to an existing readable file before proceeding; if the env var is missing or the file check fails, log a clear error and exit/throw so you don't pass undefined to the Deepgram mock or let fake audio capture fail silently. Update runTests to check process.env.DEEPGRAM_API_KEY and use fs.existsSync or fs.promises.access on audioFile, and stop execution with an explicit error message that references DEEPGRAM_API_KEY and test-audio.wav when either check fails. In `@scripts/generate_test_audio.ts`: - Line 14: The test audio generator uses sample_rate=16000 in the fetch call inside scripts/generate_test_audio.ts which conflicts with the 24000 Hz pipeline used in lib/voice/useDeepgramVoice.ts; update the Deepgram TTS request to use sample_rate=24000 (keeping encoding=linear16 if desired) so the generated audio matches the AudioContext/Deepgram input/output settings in useDeepgramVoice.ts and avoid implicit resampling; verify the URL/query string and any downstream handling still expect linear16 at 24000 Hz. --- Nitpick comments: In `@scripts/e2e.ts`: - Around line 68-73: Replace the fragile time-based hydration wait (page.waitForTimeout) with a deterministic wait: after page.goto(appUrl) use a specific readiness signal such as await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle') or await page.waitForSelector('') so tests only proceed once the app has actually hydrated; update the code around page.goto and page.waitForTimeout to call page.waitForLoadState or waitForSelector with a meaningful selector (e.g., the app root or a known hydrated element). In `@scripts/generate_test_audio.ts`: - Line 33: Top-level call to generateTestAudio() uses .catch(console.error) which logs errors but leaves process exit code as 0; change the invocation to propagate failures by handling the error and exiting with non-zero code — e.g. replace generateTestAudio().catch(console.error) with an explicit handler that logs the error (console.error or processLogger) and calls process.exit(1), or invoke generateTestAudio inside an async IIFE and catch errors to call process.exit(1); reference the generateTestAudio invocation to locate the change. ```
